atoms.b: The antagonist smiles. Only the audience sees the dagger behind his back.

wrong.text: The audience knows more than the protagonist.

wrong.text: A chef should be a great cook.

atoms.b:
“By all means, move at a glacial pace. You know how that thrills me.”
(The Devil wears Prada)

instruction.text: Choose the correct device of style and tone.

atoms.a: Don't be a Scrooge!
He's such a Romeo.
It was love at first sight.
Time flies when you're having fun.
I'm so hungry I could eat a horse!
I could sleep for a million years...

I appreciate how you're always on time!
(the person was 20 min late)

What a perfect day to go to the beach!
(the weather is looking terrible)
A traffic cop gets caught driving too fast.
A marriage counsellor files for divorce.
The audience sees the murderer hiding while detectives are still unaware about his whereabouts.
The audience knows that the accused person is innocent, but the judge doesn't yet.
In Orwell's “1984”, the Ministry of Truth spreads lies and rewrites history.
It was the best of times, it was the worst of times. (Dickens, A Tale of Two Cities)
Do I look like I was born yesterday?
Need I say more?

We had a little bit of rain.

(said after a massive storm)

I did alright...
(said after finishing the race in 1st place)
Time flies like an arrow; fruit flies like a banana.
I'm reading a book on anti-gravity. I can't put it down.
